title: Q1 2027 Roadmap Launch Readiness + Incident Review
summary: Internal roadmap and launch readiness sync for Q1 2027 with an incident review from the 12/22 outage. Agree on gating criteria, finalize runbooks, and assign postmortem actions to close telemetry and rollout gaps.

Rollout plan: canary thresholds, fallback policies

Owner: Diego - Lock down canary rollout policy and autoscale guardrails for Dedicated pools (due: 2027-01-07)
Owner: Sofia - Draft customer-facing incident summary and postmortem FAQ (due: 2027-01-04)
Owner: Ava - Share go/no-go checklist with GTM and ops and schedule final readiness meeting (due: 2027-01-06)

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-28
Time: 09:30 - 10:45 UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen, Diego Martinez, Priya Kapoor, Liam O'Neill, Sofia Ramirez, Tom Wallace, Maya Singh, Jordan Lee
Notes: internal roadmap + incident review from 2026-12-22 outage; many action items assigned.

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
- Quick recap of the 12/22 region partial outage, suspected cascade from cache miss storms and autoscaler interactions.
- Reviewed launch gating criteria for Q1 feature rollout (canary percentages, latency SLOs, ops readiness).
- Identified missing alerts and runbook steps; assigned owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava (PM): okay, um, thanks everyone for joining, we're on a tight schedule, so I'll go quickly, this is the Q1 roadmap launch readiness and we also need to go through the incident review from last week, the 12/22 partial outage, so first up who wants to take 30 seconds to call out the high-level ask — Diego?
[00:18] Diego (Eng): yeah, thanks, um, high level for eng is we need the launch gating criteria nailed down, specifically around Dedicated pool autoscale and the canary thresholds, we saw during the outage that our autoscaler oscillated when a KV cache miss storm hit the inference nodes, so we need firm thresholds and a fallback.
[00:36] Priya (Staff Eng): and to add, there were a bunch of small config mismatches between staging and prod, the quantization profile on a few model variants was different, which made one of the variants slightly slower — might be transcription, latency was higher and then the autoscaler saw higher CPU and... spiked.
[00:55] Liam (SRE): yes, and our alerts are noisy; we didn't have a good hit-rate alert for the prefix KV cache, we only had latency and GPU utilization which is lagging. so first thing is add a cache-hit-rate alert and a degraded throughput paging policy.
[01:12] Sofia (UX): quick reminder — any customer visible change needs a KB and an in-product banner that's coordinated with comms, especially for Dedicated or Private customers.
[01:25] Tom (VP Eng): ok, good, can we put an explicit go/no-go checklist on the calendar, I want to see clear owners and metrics, also is SOC two docs ready for customers that ask about audit logs?
[01:40] Maya (PM): SOC two, yes, legal has the SOC 2 pack updated but we should double-check retention windows for audit logs in Private deployments, some customers asked about KMS/HSM integration with our private plane — sorry, private plane, private control plane.
[02:02] Jordan (Release): timeline check — we are targeting early Feb for the initial rollout, what's the earliest we can run a full canary?
[02:10] Ava: we want a canary next week in staging, and then a production canary the week after if all go/no-go criteria pass. criteria being: latency p95 < 250ms on golden tests, no more than 0.5% error rate, prefix cache hit-rate above 92% for 10m window, and no pageable SRE alerts.
[02:34] Diego: those numbers sound reasonable, question — the 92% cache hit threshold, is that for aggregated traffic or per-model?
[02:44] Priya: ideally per-model, because some models have much higher cold start patterns, but for rollout gating we can start with aggregate and then refine after the canary.
[03:02] Ava: ok aggregate for canary gating, we'll add per-model checks in follow-ups.
[03:10] 
[03:20] Incident review segment (12/22 outage)
[03:22] Liam: quick timeline — at ~11:07 UTC we started seeing increased latency in us-west-2 region, by 11:10 the autoscaler started adding pods, at 11:12 we saw a cache miss burst that caused downstream CPU pressure and the autoscaler overshot. by 11:18 some nodes started OOMing and we routed traffic away but there was a secondary regression when fallback model variant was slower and caused more waiting.
[03:48] Diego: root cause seems multi-factor: cache coldness after a deployment, a recently changed kernel param for our inference runtime, and a misapplied autoscaling policy that used CPU > 70% for scale-up which is too sensitive.
[04:02] Priya: note on the runtime kernel change — it was intended to reduce memory overhead for quantized paths, but the change regressed some attention kernels for long sequences, so latency increased on a subset of sequences.
[04:20] Ava: ok, so tech fixes, policy fixes, and observability fixes. let's break those out.
[04:28] 
[04:40] Questions / chatter (some overlapping speech, transcription imperfect):
[04:42] Speaker 1: so would enabling more aggressive KV cache pre-warm address this?
[04:47] Priya: yes, we can prewarm common prefixes and tune the eviction, I can add a prewarm job in the next sprint, but we also need to ensure staging mirrors prod traffic mix, we had differences.
[05:02] Diego: and to be clear, the autoscaler policy needs hysteresis, not just threshold, so scale-up should require sustained >X for Y seconds, and scale-down longer window so we don't thrash.
[05:20] Liam: agreed, adding a 60s sustained for scale-up and 5m for scale-down is a good starting point. we'll test in staging.
[05:30] 
[05:55] Action item assignment quick-fire:
[05:57] Ava: Priya will own runbook updates, Liam owns alerts, Diego will own canary policy and autoscaler guardrails, Sofia will draft comms, I'll assemble the go/no-go checklist and own scheduling. all agreed?
[06:12] Group: yes / mm-hmm / yep
[06:20] 
[06:30] Deep dive on telemetry gaps
[06:33] Liam: two gaps we found — no direct metric for in-memory KV cache hit-rate per node, and we don't have synthetic golden tests that exercise the cold path for each model variant. both are essential for pre-launch safety.
[06:49] Priya: for the per-node metric we can instrument the runtime to emit hit/miss counters and expose them via our metric endpoint, added overhead should be minimal. I estimate a small patch and a deploy to staging by Jan 2.
[07:05] Diego: and we need dashboards and a pager path. Liam, do you want to own the dashboard?
[07:10] Liam: yes, will add dashboard with 1m and 5m views and a HitRate alert, and set page to on-call if hit-rate falls below threshold for 10m.
[07:20] 
[07:35] Notes on rollout and fallback policies
[07:37] Diego: fallback needs to be fast — if the canary fails we should automatically route to a smaller footprint model variant in the same region rather than failover to another region which increases latency. also we need to test model runtime variants (int8 vs fp16) because quantization differences caused perf variance.
[07:55] Priya: yes, and we should include a compatibility matrix for quantized variants in the runbook.
[08:03] Ava: Jordan, can Release coordinate a scheduled simulated failover test in the staging-Dedicated pool next Tuesday?
[08:10] Jordan: yes, we'll schedule it and invite SRE, eng, and PMs.
[08:16] 
[08:25] Comms and docs
[08:27] Sofia: I'll draft the customer-facing incident summary and an internal FAQ, will share the first draft by Monday. should we post a KB update for runbook changes too?
[08:36] Ava: yes, link KB and runbook in the same release notes. also include a short blurb for Sales about how we handle fallbacks and data retention.
[08:47] 
[08:55] Misc (transcription shows some filler and slight misnames):
[08:57] Speaker 2: the private plane — private control plane — KMS integration question, we need to check HSM support in the on-prem package.
[09:08] Maya: legal is running through the retention and KMS docs, I'll sync with security for the HSM ask.
[09:14] 
[09:20] Final recap and next steps
[09:21] Ava: to recap — action items assigned: Priya runbook, Liam alerts/dashboard, Diego canary/autoscale policy, Sofia comms, Ava assemble checklist. runbook and telemetry patches due first week of Jan, simulated canary failover in staging next Tuesday, follow-up Jan 6 for final launch decision.
[09:39] Diego: +1, and we'll put the canary metrics on the daily ops stand-up for the week after the canary.
[09:46] Tom: thanks team, want to emphasize we need the go/no-go matrix in writing and that GTM needs to review the customer message before we publish.
[09:57] Ava: noted, will circulate. thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
